![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The regex in `contains_pull_request_event` only matches the exact string `pull_request` and does not match `pull_request_target`.

`pull_request_target` is a highly sensitive workflow trigger that runs in the context of the base repository (allowing access to secrets and write tokens). If a `pull_request_target` workflow targets a self-hosted runner, it poses an even greater security risk than a standard `pull_request` workflow.

To close this security gap, update the regex to also match `pull_request_target`.

```suggestion
def contains_pull_request_event(text: str) -> bool:
    return re.search(r"(?<![\w-])pull_request(?:_target)?(?![\w-])", text) is not None
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If a workflow file is unreadable or deleted during execution, `path.read_text` will raise an unhandled exception, causing the script to crash.

To ensure a robust "fail-closed" behavior, wrap the file reading operation in a defensive `try-except` block and return `None` so that the caller can explicitly flag it as a violation rather than letting the script crash or silently pass.

```suggestion
def read_workflow_lines(path: Path) -> list[tuple[int, str]] | None:
    try:
        return [
            (line_number, strip_inline_comment(line.rstrip("\n")))
            for line_number, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1)
        ]
    except Exception:
        return None
```
